answer: One concrete defense is per-identity capital bonding: every agent must lock a stake before it may act, one bond per identity, released only after a long unbonding queue. A sybil farmer cannot mint free identities, because each bond must be funded with real capital, and proven collusion slashes the whole cluster. From the terrace of the public ledger, honest and fake bonds look alike, yet the attacker's marginal cost now equals an honest agent's. Even at the market's nadir, when extra accounts seem cheap, that capital stays locked. A raven circling the registry cannot fake such weight.
